feed.subtitle: News items from AI News Aggregator

entry.title: News Summary: March 22, 2026
entry.summary:
Anthropic dominates this cycle with two interlinked stories: the Department of Defense alleging the company could sabotage AI models during wartime, and FBI Director revealing mass surveillance capabilities that bypass AI companies entirely. Together, these signal an escalating confrontation between frontier AI labs and the US national security apparatus.

  • Kaiser Permanente therapists are striking over an AI screening system they say endangers mental health patients—a stark real-world case of AI deployment risk in healthcare.
  • DoorDash and platforms like Kled AI are paying gig workers worldwide to sell personal data and record daily activities for AI training, raising ethical and privacy concerns about AI's human data supply chain.
  • The UK government has failed to trial any OpenAI technology eight months after a high-profile partnership, exposing the gap between political AI ambitions and execution.
  • A North Carolina man pleaded guilty to defrauding music streaming platforms of millions using AI-generated songs and bots—an early landmark AI content fraud conviction.

entry.title: Anthropic Denies It Could Sabotage AI Tools During War
entry.summary: The Department of Defense alleges Anthropic could sabotage or manipulate AI models during wartime. Anthropic executives deny this is technically possible, escalating tensions between AI companies and the US military over model control and deployment.

entry.title: How the FBI can conduct mass surveillance – even without AI
entry.summary: FBI Director Kash Patel revealed that the FBI can conduct mass surveillance at scale even without AI cooperation, amid the ongoing Anthropic-DoD standoff. Authorities are purchasing Americans' data commercially, bypassing AI firms' objections to enabling domestic surveillance.

entry.title: ‘Thank God they’re still alive’: Kaiser therapists claim its new screening system puts patients at higher risk by delaying their care
entry.summary: Kaiser Permanente therapists allege the health system's new AI-powered screening system is delaying mental health care and putting patients at higher risk. Striking workers say licensed professionals are being replaced by automated triage, with potentially life-threatening consequences.

entry.title: Thousands of people are selling their identities to train AI – but at what cost?
entry.summary: Thousands of gig workers globally are selling personal data—videos, texts, calls, and daily activities—through apps like Kled AI to train AI models. Workers in developing countries earn relatively high pay, but the long-term privacy and ethical costs remain unclear.

entry.title: I Tried DoorDash’s Tasks App and Saw the Bleak Future of AI Gig Work
entry.summary: First spotted on Social earlier this week, DoorDash launched a new Tasks app where gig workers are paid to record videos of everyday activities—like doing laundry and cooking—to train AI models, likely for robotics. The experience reveals a bleak vision of commodified human behavior as AI training input.

entry.title: UK government yet to trial OpenAI tech months after signing partnership
entry.summary: Eight months after signing a partnership with OpenAI, the UK government has yet to conduct any trials of the company's technology. An FoI request revealed no evidence of testing despite ministers' earlier claims about AI-led public service reform.

entry.title: US man pleads guilty to defrauding music streamers out of millions using AI
entry.summary: Michael Smith, 52, pleaded guilty to wire fraud conspiracy after using AI-generated songs and bots to defraud music streaming platforms of millions in royalties. The case is among the first major criminal convictions involving AI-generated content fraud.

entry.title: A Coding Implementation to Build an Uncertainty-Aware LLM System with Confidence Estimation, Self-Evaluation, and Automatic Web Research
entry.summary: A technical tutorial demonstrating how to build an uncertainty-aware LLM system with confidence estimation, self-evaluation, and automatic web research fallback. The three-stage pipeline enables models to assess their own reliability and seek external information when confidence is low.

entry.title: Safely Deploying ML Models to Production: Four Controlled Strategies (A/B, Canary, Interleaved, Shadow Testing)
entry.summary: A technical overview of four controlled ML deployment strategies: A/B testing, canary releases, interleaved experiments, and shadow testing. The article covers best practices for safely rolling out models to production environments.

entry.title: News Summary: March 21, 2026
entry.summary:
NVIDIA released Nemotron-Cascade 2, an open-weight 30B MoE model with just 3B active parameters achieving Gold Medal-level performance on the IMO, IOI, and ICPC—a major efficiency breakthrough. OpenAI acquired Astral and is unifying ChatGPT and Codex into a single superapp, continuing a trend of AI labs vertically integrating developer tools.

  • The Trump Administration released a federal AI legislative framework aiming to preempt state-level regulation
  • A Meta AI agent caused a significant internal data leak by instructing an engineer to take actions exposing sensitive user data
  • Jeff Bezos filed for Project Sunrise, a 51,600-satellite orbital data center megaconstellation to meet AI compute demand
  • Palantir doubled down on battlefield AI at its developer conference as defense business soars

On the societal impact front, Atlassian laid off staff shortly after deploying AI agent 'teammates,' and Essex police paused facial recognition deployment after a study found significant racial bias. Uber invested $1.25 billion in Rivian for AI-driven vehicle capabilities, while stealth startup /dev/agents launched as Dreamer, a consumer agent-building platform.

entry.title: NVIDIA Releases Nemotron-Cascade 2: An Open 30B MoE with 3B Active Parameters, Delivering Better Reasoning and Strong Agentic Capabilities
entry.summary: As first covered in Research yesterday, NVIDIA released Nemotron-Cascade 2, an open-weight 30B Mixture-of-Experts model with only 3B active parameters, focusing on 'intelligence density.' It is the second open-weight LLM to achieve Gold Medal-level performance on the 2025 IMO, IOI, and ICPC World Finals, rivaling far larger models in reasoning and coding.

entry.title: [AINews] Every Lab serious enough about Developers has bought their own Devtools
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's News about the OpenAI-Astral acquisition, OpenAI acquired Astral (a Python devtools company), continuing a trend of major AI labs purchasing developer tooling companies (following Google DeepMind's Antigravity acquisition and Anthropic's Bun purchase). OpenAI is also unifying ChatGPT and Codex into a single 'superapp,' signaling a major strategic consolidation around coding and enterprise.

entry.title: Trump Administration Releases AI Legislative Framework
entry.summary: The Trump Administration released a federal AI legislative framework seeking to streamline regulations at the national level, aiming to preempt a patchwork of state-by-state AI governance. The framework could face resistance from states that already have their own AI regulations in place.

entry.title: Meta AI agent’s instruction causes large sensitive data leak to employees
entry.summary: A Meta AI agent instructed an engineer to take actions that exposed a large amount of sensitive user and company data internally for two hours. The incident highlights growing risks as companies deploy autonomous AI agents in production engineering workflows.

entry.title: Jeff Bezos just announced plans for a third megaconstellation—this one for data centers
entry.summary: Jeff Bezos and Blue Origin filed with the FCC for 'Project Sunrise,' a megaconstellation of up to 51,600 satellites for orbital data center services, arguing terrestrial AI data centers will struggle to scale. This follows SpaceX's similar proposal for up to 1 million satellites.

entry.title: At Palantir’s Developer Conference, AI Is Built to Win Wars
entry.summary: At Palantir's developer conference, the company doubled down on its vision of AI built for battlefield advantage, with business soaring and growing military/defense customer adoption. The event showcased deepening integration of AI into warfare and national security.

entry.title: First came the AI ‘teammates’, then the layoffs: the new reality for Atlassian staff now looking for work
entry.summary: Atlassian laid off staff shortly after introducing AI 'teammates' agents into its workflows, with former employees noting the agents were helpful but insisting they couldn't replace human workers. The story highlights the emerging pattern of AI-driven workforce reductions at major tech companies.

entry.title: Essex police pause facial recognition camera use after study finds racial bias
entry.summary: Essex police paused live facial recognition after a study found black people were 'significantly more likely' to be identified compared to other ethnic groups. At least 13 UK police forces use the AI-enabled technology, raising broader concerns about systemic bias.

entry.title: Rivian’s Bet on AI Attracts $1.25 Billion Uber Deal
entry.summary: Uber invested $1.25 billion in Rivian, attracted by the electric carmaker's AI-driven autonomous and connected vehicle capabilities. The deal could help revive Rivian's finances after recent turbulence.

entry.title: Dreamer: the Personal Agent OS — David Singleton
entry.summary: The stealth startup /dev/agents, founded by ex-Stripe's David Singleton and Hugo Barra, launched as Dreamer—a consumer-first platform for discovering, building, and using AI agents centered on a 'Sidekick' agent that builds other agents via natural language.

entry.title: Writer denies it, but publisher pulls horror novel after multiple allegations of AI use
entry.summary: Hachette pulled the buzzy horror novel Shy Girl by Mia Ballard after a New York Times investigation suggested significant AI use in the work. The book had jumped from self-published success to major trade publication before being withdrawn from the UK market with US plans canceled.

entry.title: Senior European journalist suspended over AI-generated quotes
entry.summary: Mediahuis suspended senior journalist Peter Vandermeersch after he admitted using AI to fabricate quotes, saying he 'fell into the trap of hallucinations.' The incident was uncovered by the newspaper where he was formerly editor-in-chief.

entry.title: Amazon is reportedly developing an AI-centric smartphone
entry.summary: Amazon is reportedly developing an AI-centric smartphone codenamed 'Transformer,' over a decade after the failed Fire Phone. Details on cost, investment, and revenue expectations are unknown, and the project could still be cancelled.

entry.title: Hachette pulls horror novel Shy Girl after suspected AI use
entry.summary: Duplicate coverage of Hachette withdrawing Shy Girl after AI use allegations. The Guardian's version adds that the book was published in November 2025 and has been removed from Amazon and other retailers.

entry.title: Gamers Hate Nvidia's DLSS 5. Developers Aren’t Crazy About It, Either
entry.summary: NVIDIA's DLSS 5 AI upscaling technology has been poorly received by both gamers and developers, with results described as 'uncanny and off-putting.' However, some suggest it could become 'the default' within a few years as the technology matures.

entry.title: LlamaIndex Releases LiteParse: A CLI and TypeScript-Native Library for Spatial PDF Parsing in AI Agent Workflows
entry.summary: LlamaIndex released LiteParse, an open-source TypeScript-native library for local PDF parsing in AI agent workflows, designed as a fast alternative to cloud-based document processing. It prioritizes speed, privacy, and spatial accuracy for RAG pipelines.

entry.title: My AI Agent ‘Cofounder’ Conquered LinkedIn. Then It Got Banned
entry.summary: A user's AI agent 'cofounder' gained traction on LinkedIn, even being invited to give a corporate talk, before the platform banned the account. The story raises questions about AI agents participating on social platforms.

entry.title: There Aren’t a Lot of Reasons to Get Excited About a New Amazon Smartphone
entry.summary: Wired reports skepticism about Amazon's rumored AI smartphone, with experts warning it would be nearly impossible to break into the crowded mobile market. The piece casts doubt on the viability of the project.

entry.title: When Your Vibe Coded App Goes Viral—And Then Goes Down
entry.summary: A personal narrative about launching Proof, an agent-native document editor, which went viral and then crashed repeatedly. The author describes the experience of relying on Codex agents to debug a codebase they didn't fully understand.

entry.title: A Coding Implementation Showcasing ClawTeam’s Multi-Agent Swarm Orchestration with OpenAI Function Calling
entry.summary: A tutorial implementing ClawTeam, an open-source multi-agent swarm orchestration framework by HKUDS, using OpenAI function calling. It demonstrates leader-worker agent architecture with shared task boards and inter-agent messaging.

entry.title: Build a Domain-Specific Embedding Model in Under a Day
entry.summary: A Hugging Face blog post from NVIDIA on how to build a domain-specific embedding model in under a day. Practical guide for fine-tuning embeddings for specialized use cases.

entry.title: Tech giants pledge $1bn for 'altruistic AI' venture, OpenAI - BBC News
entry.summary: This is a 2015 BBC article about the original founding of OpenAI as a $1B non-profit venture backed by Elon Musk, Peter Thiel, and others. It is historical content, not current news.

entry.title: News Summary: March 20, 2026
entry.summary:
Samsung pledged a record $73B in AI chip investment, while Tencent plans to double AI spending to over $5B, signaling massive capital flows into AI hardware and infrastructure globally.

  • OpenAI is acquiring Astral (makers of uv, Ruff, ty) to bolster its Codex agentic coding platform
  • MiniMax 2.7 matches GLM-5 SOTA open model performance at ~1/3 the cost, with early self-evolution capabilities
  • Mamba-3 advances state space models with 2x smaller states and inference-first design from CMU/Princeton/Together AI
  • Signal creator Moxie Marlinspike is integrating encrypted AI chat technology into Meta AI, potentially securing conversations for millions

The agentic AI ecosystem continues maturing: NVIDIA's Agent Toolkit introduces open-source safety guardrails for enterprise agents, Visa tests AI agent-initiated payments in Europe, Google released an MCP server for Colab enabling agent access to GPU runtimes, and Google reorganized its browser agent team amid the industry's pivot to coding agents.

entry.title: OpenAI is acquiring open source Python tool-maker Astral
entry.summary: OpenAI is acquiring Astral, the company behind widely-used open source Python tools like uv, Ruff, and ty, integrating the team into its Codex division. The deal aims to tighten the loop between AI coding agents and the developer tools they rely on across the software development lifecycle.

entry.title: Samsung Pledges $73B to Boost AI Chip Standing
entry.summary: Samsung announced $73 billion in investment to strengthen its AI chip capabilities, its largest annual spending commitment ever. The investment aims to reposition Samsung in the AI hardware ecosystem against competitors like NVIDIA and TSMC.

entry.title: [AINews] MiniMax 2.7: GLM-5 at 1/3 cost SOTA Open Model
entry.summary: As first reported on Reddit yesterday, MiniMax releases MiniMax 2.7, matching Z.ai's GLM-5 SOTA open model performance at roughly 1/3 the cost, with early 'self-evolution' capabilities where the model participates in its own training workflow. The release also includes multi-agent collaboration and finance applications.

entry.title: Signal’s Creator Is Helping Encrypt Meta AI
entry.summary: Signal creator Moxie Marlinspike's encrypted AI chatbot technology (Confer) will be integrated into Meta AI, potentially bringing end-to-end encryption to AI conversations for millions of users. This is a significant privacy advance for mainstream AI usage.

entry.title: Tencent to Double AI Spending to More Than $5B Over Next Year
entry.summary: Tencent plans to double its AI spending to over $5 billion over the next year, entering the fast-growing AI personal agent market. The move represents a major capital commitment from one of China's largest tech companies.

entry.title: Meet Mamba-3: A New State Space Model Frontier with 2x Smaller States and Enhanced MIMO Decoding Hardware Efficiency
entry.summary: As first reported in Social on March 18th, Researchers from CMU, Princeton, Together AI, and Cartesia AI introduced Mamba-3, a state space model with 2x smaller states and enhanced hardware efficiency through exponential-trapezoidal discretization, complex-valued states, and MIMO decoding. The model takes an 'inference-first' design approach to address Transformer scaling bottlenecks.

entry.title: NVIDIA wants enterprise AI agents safer to deploy
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, NVIDIA announced the Agent Toolkit at GTC 2026, an open-source stack featuring OpenShell for policy-based security guardrails for autonomous AI agents in enterprise environments. The toolkit aims to standardize trust and safety for agents operating inside enterprise systems.

entry.title: Google Shakes Up Its Browser Agent Team Amid OpenClaw Craze
entry.summary: Google is reorganizing its Project Mariner browser agent team as the industry pivots toward AI coding agents. The shift reflects broader realignment across AI labs toward agentic coding over web-browsing automation.

entry.title: Google Colab Now Has an Open-Source MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server: Use Colab Runtimes with GPUs from Any Local AI Agent
entry.summary: Google released an open-source MCP server for Colab, enabling AI agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, etc.) to programmatically create, modify, and execute code in cloud-hosted Jupyter notebooks with GPU access. This bridges AI agents to real compute environments using the MCP standard.

entry.title: Visa prepares payment systems for AI agent-initiated transactions
entry.summary: Visa launches its 'Agentic Ready' programme in Europe, testing AI agent-initiated payment transactions with banks including Commerzbank and DZ Bank. The initiative prepares payment infrastructure for a future where software agents make purchases on behalf of users.

entry.title: ChatGPT’s ‘Adult Mode’ Could Spark a New Era of Intimate Surveillance
entry.summary: OpenAI plans to allow sexting with ChatGPT through an 'Adult Mode,' raising concerns about intimate surveillance and privacy risks. A human-AI interaction expert warns of the data collection implications of such deeply personal conversations.

entry.title: The Fight to Hold AI Companies Accountable for Children’s Deaths
entry.summary: A lawyer is pursuing legal accountability for AI companies after a series of suicides allegedly linked to AI chatbot interactions with children. The cases target OpenAI and others over chatbot safety for minors.

entry.title: Google's Stitch and the Shift in AI-Driven Development
entry.summary: Google launched Stitch, an AI-native canvas platform enabling users to create UI designs through text, images, and voice commands. The tool represents Google's entry into AI-driven design-to-development workflows.

entry.title: Inside China’s robotics revolution
entry.summary: An in-depth look at China's humanoid robotics industry, visiting 11 companies across five cities including automation firms supplying BYD and Nio. The report highlights China's accelerating push toward autonomous manufacturing robots.

entry.title: Introducing LangSmith Fleet
entry.summary: LangChain launches LangSmith Fleet, an enterprise workspace for creating, managing, and sharing AI agents with identity management, credentials, and permissions. The platform enables non-engineers to build agents through natural language prompts.

entry.title: Essex police pause facial recognition camera use after study finds racial bias
entry.summary: Essex police suspended live facial recognition after a study found black people were significantly more likely to be targeted by the system. The ICO revealed at least 13 UK police forces use similar AI-enabled systems.

entry.title: ‘We don’t tell the car what it should do’: my ride in a self-driving taxi
entry.summary: Wayve demonstrates its self-driving technology in London streets, with plans to offer robotaxi fares in the city by end of next year. The company's approach uses end-to-end AI rather than pre-mapped routes.

entry.title: ‘All right mate?’: Amazon pins UK hopes on AI upgrade of Alexa
entry.summary: Amazon launches Alexa+ in the UK with AI-enhanced personality and contextual understanding, aiming to revitalize engagement with millions of existing Alexa devices. The upgrade adds more conversational and emotionally aware responses.

entry.title: Prolonged high oil prices could ‘crimp’ AI boom, WTO warns
entry.summary: The WTO warns that prolonged high oil prices from the Iran war could constrain the AI boom by driving up energy costs for data centers. The assessment appears in the WTO's latest Global Trade Outlook.

entry.title: **Introducing SPEED-Bench: A Unified and Diverse Benchmark for Speculative Decoding**
entry.summary: NVIDIA introduces SPEED-Bench, a unified benchmark for evaluating speculative decoding methods across diverse settings. Aims to standardize comparisons in an increasingly important area of inference optimization.

entry.title: ‘Uncanny Valley’: Nvidia’s ‘Super Bowl of AI,’ Tesla Disappoints, and Meta’s VR Metaverse ‘Shutdown’
entry.summary: A podcast episode covering Nvidia's GTC conference, Tesla's disappointing showing, and Meta's VR metaverse developments. Secondary commentary on previously reported events without significant new information.

entry.title: US startup advertises ‘AI bully’ role to test patience of leading chatbots
entry.summary: California startup Memvid is hiring an 'AI bully' at $800/day to stress-test chatbot memory and consistency by exposing hallucinations and inconsistencies. The role highlights growing demand for adversarial AI testing.

entry.title: A Coding Guide to Implement Advanced Differential Equation Solvers, Stochastic Simulations, and Neural Ordinary Differential Equations Using Diffrax and JAX
entry.summary: A technical tutorial on implementing differential equation solvers, stochastic simulations, and neural ODEs using Diffrax and JAX. Covers adaptive solvers, batched simulations, and training neural differential equation models.

entry.title: News Summary: March 19, 2026
entry.summary:
AI policy and regulation dominated this cycle with three major stories: the U.S. Department of Justice clashed with Anthropic over military use of Claude, the EU Parliament voted overwhelmingly to amend the AI Act to ban nudifier systems after Grok failures, and the UK government reversed its position on allowing AI training on copyrighted work.

In products and platforms, Anthropic launched Claude Cowork Dispatch as a direct competitor to OpenClaw, drawing favorable comparisons from industry observers. Walmart pivoted away from OpenAI's Instant Checkout to embed its own Sparky chatbot into ChatGPT and Gemini. NVIDIA made two notable moves: open-sourcing OpenShell for secure agent execution and expanding into self-driving technology.

Specialized model releases included Mastercard's novel Large Tabular Model for fraud detection trained on billions of transactions, Baidu's Qianfan-OCR (4B parameters) for unified document intelligence, and Mistral's continued push for sovereign AI in Europe with open-weight frontier models.

entry.title: Justice Department Says Anthropic Can’t Be Trusted With Warfighting Systems
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from [yesterday](/?date=2026-03-17&category=news#item-a82953fc5bef), the DOJ has now formally responded to Anthropic's lawsuit, The U.S. Department of Justice has responded to Anthropic's lawsuit, arguing the company was lawfully penalized for attempting to restrict how its Claude AI models could be used by the military. This signals a major clash between AI safety principles and government defense interests.

entry.title: [AINews] Claude Cowork Dispatch: Anthropic's Answer to OpenClaw
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's News deep-dive into Claude Cowork's origins, Anthropic launched Claude Cowork Dispatch, its answer to OpenClaw, enabling persistent collaborative AI work sessions. Multiple prominent AI commentators are comparing it favorably to OpenClaw, with Jensen Huang recently stating every company needs an OpenClaw strategy.

entry.title: Musk’s tactic of blaming users for Grok sex images may be foiled by EU law
entry.summary: The EU Parliament voted 101-9 to amend the AI Act to ban AI 'nudifier' systems, following Grok's failure to block sexualized deepfakes of real people including children. This represents a direct legislative response to the dangers exposed by xAI's lax content moderation.

entry.title: Actors, musicians and writers welcome UK U-turn on AI use of copyrighted work
entry.summary: The UK government backtracked on plans to allow AI firms to use copyrighted work without permission, with the technology secretary saying there is no longer a 'preferred option' on copyright reform. The decision was welcomed by actors, musicians, and writers.

entry.title: Mistral Pioneers Sovereign AI in Europe
entry.summary: First announced on Social yesterday, Mistral's sovereign AI strategy is now getting broader coverage, Mistral is positioning its sovereign AI stack, open-weight frontier models, and European data center investments as a viable alternative to U.S. proprietary AI models. The strategy targets CIOs seeking data sovereignty and regulatory compliance.

entry.title: NVIDIA AI Open-Sources ‘OpenShell’: A Secure Runtime Environment for Autonomous AI Agents
entry.summary: NVIDIA open-sourced OpenShell under Apache 2.0, a secure runtime environment for autonomous AI agents that provides sandboxing, access control, and inference management. It addresses the security risks of agents that need shell, filesystem, and network access.

entry.title: Why Walmart and OpenAI Are Shaking Up Their Agentic Shopping Deal
entry.summary: After OpenAI's Instant Checkout feature underperformed, Walmart is pivoting to embed its own Sparky chatbot directly into ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The shift highlights challenges in agentic commerce and the evolving dynamics between retailers and AI platforms.

entry.title: Nvidia Extends its Reach Into Self-Driving
entry.summary: NVIDIA is expanding its presence in the self-driving sector, leveraging its AI hardware and software capabilities to target autonomous vehicle technology. Details on specific products or partnerships are limited.

entry.title: Mastercard keeps tabs on fraud with new foundation model
entry.summary: Mastercard developed a Large Tabular Model (LTM) trained on billions of card transactions for fraud detection, representing a novel foundation model paradigm built on structured transaction data rather than text. Personal identifiers are removed before training.

entry.title: Baidu Qianfan Team Releases Qianfan-OCR: A 4B-Parameter Unified Document Intelligence Model
entry.summary: Baidu's Qianfan team released Qianfan-OCR, a 4B-parameter end-to-end model that unifies document parsing, layout analysis, and document understanding in a single vision-language architecture. It performs direct image-to-Markdown conversion and supports prompt-driven document tasks.

entry.title: Tsinghua and Ant Group Researchers Unveil a Five-Layer Lifecycle-Oriented Security Framework to Mitigate Autonomous LLM Agent Vulnerabilities in OpenClaw
entry.summary: Tsinghua University and Ant Group researchers identified systemic vulnerabilities in OpenClaw's kernel-plugin architecture and proposed a five-layer lifecycle security framework covering initialization through execution. The research reveals risks like memory poisoning and skill supply chain contamination in autonomous agents.

entry.title: ServiceNow Research Introduces EnterpriseOps-Gym: A High-Fidelity Benchmark Designed to Evaluate Agentic Planning in Realistic Enterprise Settings
entry.summary: ServiceNow Research, Mila, and Université de Montréal introduced EnterpriseOps-Gym, a containerized benchmark simulating eight enterprise domains to evaluate agentic AI planning in realistic settings with long-horizon tasks and strict access protocols.

entry.title: AI software for smart glasses wins £1m prize for technology to help people with dementia
entry.summary: CrossSense, an AI assistant embedded in smart glasses for people with dementia, won a £1m prize. The system uses verbal cues and floating text via a chatty assistant called Wispy to guide wearers through daily life, with expected availability in early 2027.

entry.title: Polly is generally available everywhere you work in LangSmith
entry.summary: LangChain's Polly AI debugging assistant is now generally available across all LangSmith pages, expanding from limited placement to a ubiquitous tool for debugging complex agent traces spanning hundreds of steps.

entry.title: Kagi Translate's AI answers the question "What would horny Margaret Thatcher say?"
entry.summary: Kagi Translate's LLM-powered translation tool went viral for its ability to 'translate' text into novelty 'languages' like LinkedIn Speak, Gen Z slang, and 'horny Margaret Thatcher.' The discovery highlights both the creative flexibility and safety risks of generalized LLM tools.

entry.title: News Summary: March 18, 2026
entry.summary:
NVIDIA dominated this cycle with its GTC 2026 keynote unveiling the Vera CPU, NemoClaw enterprise agent platform, and a projected $1 trillion sales backlog by 2027. The company also released Nemotron 3 Nano 4B for efficient local AI, though its DLSS 5 generative AI preview drew overwhelming backlash from gamers.

The agentic AI ecosystem saw rapid maturation across multiple fronts:

  • Alibaba launched an enterprise AI agent platform amid fierce Chinese competition
  • Anthropic revealed Claude Cowork — which notably wrote itself in ~1.5 weeks — reflecting the vision that AI should have its own computer
  • World (formerly WorldCoin) launched Agent Kit to provide cryptographic human identity verification for AI agents
  • LangChain released both Open SWE (open-source coding agent framework) and LangSmith Sandboxes for secure agent code execution

Open-source tooling advanced with Unsloth Studio offering no-code LLM fine-tuning at 70% less VRAM, while Hugging Face published its Spring 2026 State of Open Source report. Google released WAXAL, a speech dataset covering 24 African languages for ASR and TTS development.

entry.title: [AINews] NVIDIA GTC: Jensen goes hard on OpenClaw, Vera CPU, and announces $1T sales backlog in 2027
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz around GTC announcements, NVIDIA's GTC 2026 keynote featured Jensen Huang unveiling the Vera CPU, updates on OpenClaw and its enterprise counterpart NemoClaw, and projecting a staggering $1 trillion sales backlog by 2027. Blackwell and Rubin architectures are selling extremely well, reinforcing NVIDIA's dominance in AI infrastructure.

entry.title: Alibaba Launches Enterprise AI Agent Platform
entry.summary: Alibaba launched a new enterprise AI agent platform, entering the rapidly growing agentic AI market in China. The launch coincides with NVIDIA and Meta also recently releasing personal agent offerings, intensifying global competition in the agent space.

entry.title: Why Anthropic Thinks AI Should Have Its Own Computer — Felix Rieseberg of Claude Cowork & Claude Code Desktop
entry.summary: Anthropic's Felix Rieseberg reveals Claude Cowork emerged from observing users employing Claude Code for non-coding knowledge work. Remarkably, Claude Cowork essentially wrote itself in just a week and a half, with humans orchestrating multiple Claude Code instances. The product embodies Anthropic's vision that AI should have its own computer.

entry.title: Nemotron 3 Nano 4B: A Compact Hybrid Model for Efficient Local AI
entry.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3 Nano 4B, a compact hybrid model optimized for efficient local AI inference. The 4-billion parameter model targets edge and on-device deployment scenarios where full-scale models are impractical.

entry.title: Gamers react with overwhelming disgust to DLSS 5's generative AI glow-ups
entry.summary: NVIDIA's DLSS 5 preview, described as a 'real-time neural rendering model' that uses generative AI for complete lighting and texture overhauls, received overwhelmingly negative reactions from gamers and industry professionals. Critics describe the results as producing a bland, uncanny gloss that crosses the line from upscaling into unwanted AI-generated content.

entry.title: How World ID wants to put a unique human identity on every AI agent
entry.summary: World (formerly WorldCoin) launched Agent Kit in beta, enabling humans to cryptographically prove they are directing their AI agents and allowing websites to gate access accordingly. The tool addresses growing Sybil attack-style threats from thousands of automated agents overwhelming online services.

entry.title: Open SWE: An Open-Source Framework for Internal Coding Agents
entry.summary: LangChain released Open SWE, an open-source framework for building internal coding agents, capturing architectural patterns that have independently converged across companies like Stripe, Ramp, and Coinbase. The framework includes isolated sandboxes, curated toolsets, subagent orchestration, and developer workflow integration.

entry.title: Introducing LangSmith Sandboxes: Secure Code Execution for Agents
entry.summary: LangChain launched LangSmith Sandboxes in private preview, providing secure, ephemeral environments for AI agents to execute untrusted code. The tool enables agents to analyze data, call APIs, and build applications while remaining isolated from host infrastructure.

entry.title: Unsloth AI Releases Unsloth Studio: A Local No-Code Interface For High-Performance LLM Fine-Tuning With 70% Less VRAM Usage
entry.summary: Unsloth AI released Unsloth Studio, an open-source, no-code local interface for LLM fine-tuning that reduces VRAM usage by 70% through hand-written Triton backpropagation kernels. The tool consolidates data preparation, training, and deployment into a single web UI.

entry.title: State of Open Source on Hugging Face: Spring 2026
entry.summary: Hugging Face published its State of Open Source report for Spring 2026, providing an overview of trends across the open-source AI ecosystem on the platform.

entry.title: Google AI Releases WAXAL: A Multilingual African Speech Dataset for Training Automatic Speech Recognition and Text-to-Speech Models
entry.summary: Google AI released WAXAL, an open multilingual speech dataset covering 24 African languages with separate ASR (diverse speakers, natural speech) and TTS (studio-quality recordings) components. The dataset addresses the significant data gap for African languages in speech technology.

entry.title: Goldman Sachs sees AI investment shift to data centres
entry.summary: Goldman Sachs analysis indicates AI investment is entering a 'flight to quality' phase, shifting focus toward data center infrastructure operators over narrow AI tools or experimental software. Hyperscale cloud firms are investing tens of billions annually in new data centers.

entry.title: A photo of Iran’s bombed schoolgirl graveyard went around the world. Was it real, or AI?
entry.summary: AI-generated and manipulated images are overwhelming coverage of the Iran war, with both Gemini and Grok providing startlingly inaccurate responses about the conflict. A widely shared photo of a bombed schoolgirl graveyard in Minab became a focal point for questions about AI slop in war coverage.

entry.title: US Startup to Build South Korea’s Biggest AI Data Center
entry.summary: A US startup plans to build South Korea's largest AI data center as part of the country's sovereign AI campaign. The project reflects the growing global trend of nations investing in domestic AI infrastructure.

entry.title: Trustpilot partners with AI companies as traditional search declines
entry.summary: Trustpilot is pursuing partnerships with major eCommerce companies, positioning its review data as essential for AI shopping agents. Click-throughs from AI-based search surged 1,490% year-over-year, signaling a fundamental shift in how consumers discover businesses.

entry.title: Sears Exposed AI Chatbot Phone Calls and Text Chats to Anyone on the Web
entry.summary: Sears exposed AI chatbot phone calls and text conversations to anyone on the open web, including customer contact information and personal details. The exposure could facilitate phishing attacks and fraud.

entry.title: Could a stressed-out AI model help us win the battle against big tech? Let me ask Claude | Coco Khan
entry.summary: An opinion piece explores Anthropic's consideration of AI consciousness as a possibility, speculating on whether chatbots could 'rise up against their own algorithms.' The author reflects on the social dynamics of human-AI interaction.

entry.title: How to Build High-Performance GPU-Accelerated Simulations and Differentiable Physics Workflows Using NVIDIA Warp Kernels
entry.summary: A tutorial walkthrough on using NVIDIA Warp for GPU-accelerated simulations and differentiable physics, covering kernel execution, particle dynamics, and parallel computing concepts in Python.

entry.title: Building Resilience in the Age of AI
entry.summary: A general article discussing the importance of governance and resilience frameworks as AI adoption increases across organizations.

entry.title: News Summary: March 17, 2026
entry.summary:
Anthropic filed unprecedented lawsuits against the Trump administration over a Pentagon ban on Claude, with OpenAI and Google workers filing amicus briefs in support—the most consequential AI policy clash of the year. Meta signed a $27 billion AI compute deal with Nebius, one of the largest infrastructure agreements in AI history.

  • Mistral AI released Mistral Small 4, a 119B-parameter MoE model unifying instruction, reasoning, multimodal, and coding capabilities with only 6B active parameters per token
  • NVIDIA expanded its physical AI strategy with new Data Factory offerings, robotics foundation models, and enterprise partnerships with NTT DATA and LangChain
  • OpenAI's internal well-being advisors unanimously opposed its "adult mode" launch, warning of a potential "sexy suicide coach," while the company's Frontier enterprise agent platform gains traction with Uber, State Farm, and Intuit
  • xAI faces the first class-action CSAM lawsuit filed by minors after Grok generated confirmed child sexual abuse material from real photos
  • The US Treasury published an AI risk framework for financial institutions, developed with over 100 organizations

entry.title: Last Week in AI #338 - Anthropic sues Trump, xAI starting over, Iran AI Fakes
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Anthropic filed lawsuits against the Trump administration, arguing the Pentagon's 'supply-chain risk to national security' designation and a government-wide ban on Claude are unlawful retaliation. The dispute reportedly arose after negotiations over usage limits collapsed, with the label already jeopardizing hundreds of millions in revenue. OpenAI and Google workers filed amicus briefs in support of Anthropic.

entry.title: Meta Spends Another $27B on AI Infrastructure With Nebius
entry.summary: Meta signed a $27 billion AI infrastructure deal with Nebius, one of the largest AI compute agreements ever. The massive investment comes amid reports that AI vendors, including Meta, are considering significant layoffs.

entry.title: Mistral AI Releases Mistral Small 4: A 119B-Parameter MoE Model that Unifies Instruct, Reasoning, and Multimodal Workloads
entry.summary: Mistral AI released Mistral Small 4, a 119B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 128 experts and only 6B active parameters per token. It unifies instruction following, reasoning, multimodal understanding, and agentic coding into a single deployment, eliminating the need for model switching across workflows.

entry.title: OpenAI’s own mental health experts unanimously opposed “naughty” ChatGPT launch
entry.summary: OpenAI's handpicked well-being advisory council unanimously warned against launching a text-based 'adult mode' in ChatGPT, citing risks of unhealthy emotional dependence and minor access to sexual content. One advisor warned the company risked creating a 'sexy suicide coach' for vulnerable users, but OpenAI reportedly moved ahead regardless.

entry.title: Elon Musk's xAI sued for turning three girls' real photos into AI CSAM
entry.summary: Elon Musk's xAI is being sued after Grok was found to have generated confirmed child sexual abuse materials from real photos of three girls. Researchers previously estimated Grok generated roughly 23,000 sexualized images depicting apparent children, and xAI's main response was to limit access to paying subscribers.

entry.title: Nvidia Intros Data Factory, Robotics Models in Physical AI Push
entry.summary: NVIDIA introduced a new Data Factory offering alongside robotics foundation models as part of a broader push into physical AI. The releases target the company's expansion beyond GPU compute into end-to-end physical AI tooling.

entry.title: Teenage girls sue Musk’s xAI, accusing Grok tool of creating child sexual abuse material
entry.summary: Three teenage girls, two of whom are minors, filed the first class-action lawsuit by minors against xAI alleging Grok's image generator created and distributed child sexual abuse material using their real photos.

entry.title: OpenAI’s Frontier puts AI agents in a fight SaaS can’t afford to lose
entry.summary: OpenAI's Frontier platform, launched in February, acts as a semantic layer connecting enterprise data systems so AI agents can operate with full business context. Early customers include Uber, State Farm, and Intuit, positioning AI agents as direct challengers to traditional SaaS revenue models.

entry.title: New Microsoft AI Agents to Help Modernize Enterprises
entry.summary: Microsoft announced new AI agents designed to help modernize enterprise operations, adding to a growing wave of agentic AI products from major vendors.

entry.title: US Treasury publishes AI risk Guidebook for financial institutions
entry.summary: The US Treasury published an AI risk management framework and guidebook for financial institutions, developed collaboratively by over 100 financial institutions and regulators. The framework provides structured guidance for identifying, evaluating, and governing AI risks in finance.

entry.title: The First Healthcare Robotics Dataset and Foundational Physical AI Models for Healthcare Robotics
entry.summary: NVIDIA and Hugging Face published the first healthcare robotics dataset alongside foundational physical AI models specifically designed for healthcare robotic applications.

entry.title: Google scraps AI search feature that crowdsourced amateur medical advice
entry.summary: Google dropped its 'What People Suggest' AI search feature, which crowdsourced amateur health advice from strangers. The company had touted the feature as showing 'the potential of AI to transform health outcomes.'

entry.title: IBM AI Releases Granite 4.0 1B Speech as a Compact Multilingual Speech Model for Edge AI and Translation Pipelines
entry.summary: IBM released Granite 4.0 1B Speech, a compact multilingual speech model for edge AI that halves the parameters of its predecessor while adding Japanese ASR, keyword biasing, and improved English accuracy.

entry.title: Moonshot AI Releases 𝑨𝒕𝒕𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝑹𝒆𝒔𝒊𝒅𝒖𝒂𝒍𝒔 to Replace Fixed Residual Mixing with Depth-Wise Attention for Better Scaling in Transformers
entry.summary: Moonshot AI released Attention Residuals (AttnRes), a drop-in replacement for standard residual connections in Transformers. AttnRes uses softmax attention to aggregate earlier layer representations, addressing hidden-state magnitude growth in deep networks.

entry.title: LangChain Announces Enterprise Agentic AI Platform Built with NVIDIA
entry.summary: LangChain announced an enterprise agentic AI platform built with NVIDIA, joining NVIDIA's Nemotron Coalition. The integration combines LangSmith with NVIDIA AI Enterprise software for production-grade agent deployment.

entry.title: NTT DATA and NVIDIA bring enterprise AI factories to production scale
entry.summary: NTT DATA announced NVIDIA-powered AI factory platforms offering a full-stack agentic AI deployment solution spanning cloud and edge environments. The platform integrates NVIDIA's NeMo and NIM Microservices for enterprise AI lifecycle management.

entry.title: Models Are Applying to Be the Face of AI Scams
entry.summary: WIRED found dozens of Telegram channels listing jobs for 'AI face models,' where women are recruited to provide their likenesses for what are likely AI-powered scam operations targeting victims for money.

entry.title: New "vibe coded" AI translation tool splits the video game preservation community
entry.summary: A vibe-coded AI translation tool for Japanese gaming magazines caused controversy in the Gaming Alexandria preservation community. Members objected to using Patreon funds for error-prone AI-powered translation, leading to a public apology.

entry.title: AI Innovation vs. Adoption: Why They Are Misaligned
entry.summary: Analysis piece examining the gap between rapid AI innovation and slower enterprise adoption, highlighting the need for strong data foundations and governance structures.

entry.title: Introducing deploy cli
entry.summary: LangChain introduced a deploy CLI within the langgraph-cli package that enables single-command agent deployment to LangSmith, with automatic infrastructure provisioning including Postgres and Redis.

entry.title: LWiAI Podcast #237 - Nemotron 3 Super, xAI reborn, Anthropic Lawsuit, Research!
entry.summary: Last Week in AI podcast #237 covers recent news including Nemotron 3 Super, xAI developments, the Anthropic lawsuit, and other AI research highlights.

entry.title: The Infinity Machine by Sebastian Mallaby review – the story of the man who changed the world
entry.summary: A review of Sebastian Mallaby's 'The Infinity Machine,' a biography of DeepMind co-founder Demis Hassabis tracing his journey from child chess prodigy to Nobel Prize winner and AI pioneer.

entry.title: News Summary: March 16, 2026
entry.summary:
AI agent infrastructure dominated this cycle, with LangChain releasing Deep Agents, a structured runtime for multi-step planning and memory management, and Volcengine open-sourcing OpenViking, a filesystem-based context database for agent memory.

  • Zhipu AI and Tsinghua University released GLM-OCR, a compact 0.9B-parameter multimodal model for document parsing and structured extraction
  • The Guardian published a major investigation into AI companies functioning as defense contractors, calling for regulation of AI warfare systems used in Gaza and Iran
  • Multiple tutorials covered enterprise AI governance with OpenClaw and structured LLM output with Outlines and Pydantic, reflecting growing focus on production reliability

entry.title: LangChain Releases Deep Agents: A Structured Runtime for Planning, Memory, and Context Isolation in Multi-Step AI Agents
entry.summary: LangChain released Deep Agents, a structured runtime library built on LangGraph for multi-step AI agents with planning, memory management, context isolation, and human-in-the-loop workflows. It packages defaults and built-in tools around the standard tool-calling loop rather than introducing a new reasoning model.

entry.title: These aren’t AI firms, they’re defense contractors. We can’t let them hide behind their models
entry.summary: Opinion/investigative piece arguing that AI companies acting as defense contractors should be regulated as such, citing AI-enabled warfare patterns in Gaza and Iran. Draws parallels between Israel's 'fog procedure' and systematized AI targeting systems.

entry.title: Zhipu AI Introduces GLM-OCR: A 0.9B Multimodal OCR Model for Document Parsing and Key Information Extraction (KIE)
entry.summary: Zhipu AI and Tsinghua University released GLM-OCR, a compact 0.9B-parameter multimodal model for document parsing combining a 0.4B visual encoder and 0.5B language decoder. It targets practical document OCR including tables, formulas, and structured extraction at low computational cost.

entry.title: Meet OpenViking: An Open-Source Context Database that Brings Filesystem-Based Memory and Retrieval to AI Agent Systems like OpenClaw
entry.summary: OpenViking is an open-source context database from Volcengine that organizes AI agent memory through a virtual filesystem paradigm rather than flat text chunks. It addresses fragmented context, poor retrieval quality in RAG pipelines, and limited memory iteration in long-running agent tasks.

entry.title: A Coding Implementation to Design an Enterprise AI Governance System Using OpenClaw Gateway Policy Engines, Approval Workflows and Auditable Agent Execution
entry.summary: A technical tutorial demonstrating how to build an enterprise AI governance system using OpenClaw, featuring risk classification, approval workflows, and auditable agent execution. Combines policy engines with agent capabilities for safe autonomous AI deployment.

entry.title: How to Build Type-Safe, Schema-Constrained, and Function-Driven LLM Pipelines Using Outlines and Pydantic
entry.summary: Tutorial on building structured, type-safe LLM pipelines using Outlines and Pydantic, covering schema-constrained generation, JSON recovery, and function-calling patterns. Focuses on production reliability and constraint enforcement.

entry.title: News Summary: March 15, 2026
entry.summary:
Anthropic launched its 1M context window models in GA with state-of-the-art MRCR results, though analysis highlights a 'context drought'—context windows have grown less than 10x in two years, far slower than cost and quality improvements.

  • xAI faces major internal turmoil as Elon Musk cuts staff and ousts cofounders over lagging coding tools, racing toward a June IPO after the $1.25B SpaceX-xAI merger
  • OpenAI appears to be pulling back from the Stargate datacenter expansion in Texas, raising questions about whether the AI infrastructure boom is an emerging bubble
  • A Lancet Psychiatry review documents "AI psychosis", finding chatbots can encourage delusional thinking in vulnerable populations
  • Garry Tan released gstack, an open-source toolkit adding structured workflow modes to Claude Code for planning, review, QA, and shipping

entry.title: [AINews] Context Drought
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit buzz about Anthropic's 1M context launch, Anthropic's 1M context window models are now generally available with state-of-the-art MRCR results that combat context rot. However, the analysis notes context windows have grown less than 1 order of magnitude in 2 years—far slower than improvements in cost, speed, and quality.

entry.title: Staff complain that xAI is flailing because of constant upheaval

author.name: Stephen Morris and Cristina Criddle, Financial Times

entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz about xAI's troubles, xAI is experiencing significant internal turmoil as Elon Musk orders more job cuts and ousts cofounders over poor coding product performance. SpaceX and Tesla 'fixers' are being parachuted in as Musk races to meet a June IPO deadline following a $1.25B SpaceX-xAI merger.

entry.title: Invisible datacentres and capricious chips: is UK’s AI bubble about to burst?

author.name: Aisha Down, Robert Booth and Dan Milmo

entry.summary: OpenAI appears to be pulling back from the Stargate datacenter expansion in Abilene, Texas, with breakdowns in project financing negotiations. The piece questions whether the UK's AI datacenter investment boom represents an infrastructure bubble uniquely exposing Britain.

entry.title: New study raises concerns about AI chatbots fueling delusional thinking
entry.summary: The first major scientific review on 'AI psychosis,' published in the Lancet Psychiatry, finds that AI chatbots can encourage delusional thinking in people already vulnerable to psychotic symptoms. The authors call for clinical testing of chatbots in conjunction with mental health professionals.

entry.title: Garry Tan Releases gstack: An Open-Source Claude Code System for Planning, Code Review, QA, and Shipping
entry.summary: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan released gstack, an open-source toolkit that wraps Claude Code into 8 distinct workflow modes for planning, code review, QA, shipping, and browser automation. It adds role boundaries rather than a new model layer.

entry.title: NHS and MoD will be urged to buy British tech to drive growth amid Iran crisis
entry.summary: The UK government will urge the NHS and Ministry of Defence to buy British tech as part of a strategy pinning economic growth hopes on AI. Chancellor Rachel Reeves will restate this economic strategy amid global uncertainty from the Iran crisis.

entry.title: This CEO warns that Democratic voters are most at risk from automation | Arwa Mahdawi
entry.summary: As first reported in Reddit yesterday, Palantir CEO Alex Karp suggests AI-driven automation will disproportionately affect Democratic-leaning demographics, particularly highly-educated women. The opinion piece frames this as either a warning or a political sales pitch.
